## What I often use

### `%||%`

Quoted from R base control Help documentation: 
> The null coalescing operator `%||%` is a simple 1-line function: x %||% y is an idiomatic way to call

    if (is.null(x)) y else x
                             # or equivalently, of course,
    if(!is.null(x)) x else y 
Inspired by Ruby, it was first proposed by Hadley Wickham.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
res <- {}
res %||% "alternative result"
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "alternative result"
```


:::
:::





::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(magrittr)
```
:::


## Forward-pipe operator

R now has `|>` in base. 


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
rnorm(5000) %>%
  abs %>% `*` (100)  %>%
  matrix(ncol=10)  %>%
  rowMeans %>% round %>% 
  `%%`(9) %>% hist
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](R_pipeline_operator_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


## Tee operator (left) `%T>%`


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
rnorm(5000) %>%
  abs %>% `*` (100)  %>%
  matrix(ncol=10)  %>%
  rowMeans %>% round %>% 
  `%%`(9) %T>% hist %>% sum
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](R_pipeline_operator_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=672}
:::
